canonical_data_sources.alpha_classifier_final_orphans: alpha_matches.json matches[].match_status=='unavailable' (Pure-LLM Semantic Authority has no intermediate fallback for this task -- canonical, definitive per-claim ground truth)
canonical_data_sources.evidence_stance_and_structure_extractor_: llm_semantic_calls.jsonl task/fallback_used (both tasks DO have a deterministic fallback baseline; fallback_used=True is that call's final, non-LLM outcome -- more precise than raw retry-attempt counting)
canonical_data_sources.decision_to_not_create_a_second_logging_: All required data already exists in already-persisted artifacts; no new logging/telemetry was introduced. This module is a pure read-only aggregator.

code_changes.why_a_new_module_not_an_extension_of_exi: comqutor_alpha.regression.semantic_execution_health already computes the alpha_classifier-specific coverage/health contract from alpha_matches.json and is REUSED directly (imported, not duplicated) for its semantic_execution_health_status field. It does not cover evidence_stance_classifier/structure_extractor, nor the deterministic-lineage alphas_impacted_by_provider_failure metric, nor benchmark_review_required -- the new module adds exactly that additional scope, additively. comqutor_alpha.regression.regression_report_v3 (the Gold-adjacent report generator) was deliberately left completely untouched to keep zero coupling to any Gold-result computation path, per the explicit 'must NOT change Gold results' requirement.

no_alpha_semantic_effect_proof.methodology: 1) The new module never imports alpha_mapper.py, activation_scorer_v2.py, structure_extractor.py, graph_builder.py, or pipeline.py (verified by test_l_diagnostics_module_never_imports_scoring_or_mapping_modules). 2) It only READS already-persisted JSON/JSONL files, never writes to any of them. 3) Byte-identical before/after hash checks on alpha_matches.json and structure_graph.json for all six real runs (test_l_diagnostics_do_not_mutate_*_artifact) confirm zero mutation. 4) pipeline.py and activation_scorer_v2.py (the P0/P1-patched files) are confirmed byte-identical to their pre-this-task state via direct diff against preserved backups.

null_denominator_policy: Every rate field returns None (never a guessed/fabricated value) when its denominator is unavailable or non-positive -- verified by test_i_null_denominator_returns_none_not_guessed.

provider_health_status_rule.rule: PROVIDER_DEGRADED iff provider_final_orphans_total > 0 (i.e. at least one semantic-critical final orphan exists anywhere in the run). No arbitrary numeric failure-rate threshold introduced, per explicit instruction.

benchmark_review_policy.benchmark_review_required_rule: TRUE iff alphas_impacted_by_provider_failure >= 1 (a manual-review trigger, never an automatic rejection)
benchmark_review_policy.benchmark_auto_rejected: Always False in this v0.1.3 implementation -- no automatic exclusion threshold exists yet
benchmark_review_policy.documented_policy: DEPENDS_ON_IMPACT -- manual review triggered when >=1 Alpha shows deterministic lineage-loss evidence; no automatic threshold-based exclusion yet. This is descriptive, not prescriptive: benchmark_review_required=True does not mean the run or its Gold contribution is invalid -- it means a human should apply the same claim-level lineage trace this diagnostic performed before treating an affected Alpha's miss/hit as purely algorithmic.

semantic_pass_independence.principle: semantic_status (from the existing, unmodified semantic_execution_health module) and provider_health/benchmark_review_required (from this new module) are reported side by side, never collapsed into one field.

six_run_offline_replay_summary: See docs/audit_artifacts/v0_1_3_provider_health_diagnostics.json/.md for the full per-run output. All six runs' provider_failure_events/semantic_critical_failure_events exactly match the prior blast-radius audit's regression expectations.
